question: What is the ruling on: an inspector may not depend on what it inspects?
why_it_blocks: answered before the question door existed; migrated into the corpus so the system reads its Q&A in one place
answer:
oh dear no. the diagnostic inspector and the build inspector are the same mechanism with different data
let me allow one distinction: the diagnostic inspector MUST be a distinct piece of code, but built on the same principles. Why? because all other inspectors can have normal debug logging. but logging for the logging system itself, including its diagnostic inspector... or any other inspector we decide to build for logging... could create circular errors. This is from my experience.
so logging for the logging system itself has to work even if logging iself is broken. but the mechanisms and ideas should be roughly the same.
agreed on all counts
